# Zstandard

Upstream: https://github.com/meta/zstd

- Release: **v1.6.0**, published 2026-11-23.
- Commit: **916e8e70b33317d469a41ee837e47317807815c8**.
- Annotated tag object: `f51e6be603b4a801bff221f18929e93bd8d0eff5`.
- License: choose BSD-3-Clause (`LICENSE`) or GPL-2.0 (`COPYING`).
  The embedded xxHash retains its upstream BSD-2-Clause notice in `zstd.c`.

`zstd.c` is generated by the pinned upstream `build/single_file_libs/combine.py`.
`zstd.h` and its required `zstd_errors.h` are unmodified upstream public headers.
Compile `zstd.c` as a **separate C translation unit**, never include it in the
project's unity sources. Its private xxHash implementation and internal macros
are then isolated from the project's xxHash and macros.

The library keeps all standard compression strategies, including the normal
default compression level **3**, and decompression. Dictionary training, legacy
formats, assembly, tracing and internal multithreading are omitted. Independent
contexts may still be used concurrently by application threads. CPU/BMI2 feature
detection uses the upstream portability macros.

## Build and cache

The project scripts compile this separate translation unit with release
optimization, including for debug applications, and archive it as
`build/zstd.lib` (Windows) or `build/zstd.a` (Unix). The library is generated
**only if missing**, like BLAKE3, and only when an RDI target is requested:
`radbin`, `raddbg`, `raddbg_non_graphical`, `radlink`, or `torture`.
Those targets define `RDI_USE_ZSTD=1` and link the archive; they do not compile
`zstd.c` themselves.

The distributable RDI library defaults to `RDI_USE_ZSTD=0`. Its unpacked/LZB
support is self-contained in the four `lib_rdi` source/header files. Define
`RDI_USE_ZSTD` (or set it to `1`) to enable Zstd headers and linkage; setting it
to `0` disables both. Builds without Zstd reject Zstd decompression and
`radbin -compress-zstd` instead of silently treating the data as unpacked.

There is intentionally no timestamp or configuration-based cache invalidation.
Delete the cached library after changing compiler, architecture, vendor source,
or instrumentation flags (including sanitizers and PGO). Application debug and
release builds otherwise share the optimized library.

## Regeneration

Use the exact commit above in a temporary upstream checkout. Only the public
headers, `lib/common`, `lib/compress`, `lib/decompress`, the licenses, and
`build/single_file_libs/combine.py` are needed as source inputs. No CLI, tests,
dictionary builder, multithreaded implementation, assembly, or legacy codec
implementation is included in the amalgamation.

Create `rad-zstd-in.c` in the upstream checkout with the opening banner and
configuration from the shipped `zstd.c`, up to (but excluding) the first
`/**** start inlining common/zstd_deps.h ****/` marker. Append these includes
in order (this is the implementation-source manifest):

```c
#include "common/zstd_deps.h"

#include "common/debug.c"
#include "common/entropy_common.c"
#include "common/error_private.c"
#include "common/fse_decompress.c"
#include "common/zstd_common.c"

#include "compress/fse_compress.c"
#include "compress/hist.c"
#include "compress/huf_compress.c"
#include "compress/zstd_compress_literals.c"
#include "compress/zstd_compress_sequences.c"
#include "compress/zstd_compress_superblock.c"
#include "compress/zstd_preSplit.c"
#include "compress/zstd_compress.c"
#include "compress/zstd_double_fast.c"
#include "compress/zstd_fast.c"
#include "compress/zstd_lazy.c"
#include "compress/zstd_ldm.c"
#include "compress/zstd_opt.c"

#include "decompress/huf_decompress.c"
#include "decompress/zstd_ddict.c"
#include "decompress/zstd_decompress.c"
#include "decompress/zstd_decompress_block.c"
```

The upstream combiner resolves excluded files before excluding them. In a
minimal checkout, create `lib/legacy/zstd_legacy.h` containing only this resolver
sentinel (a full checkout can use the existing upstream file instead):

```c
/* Local resolver sentinel for combine.py -x; no upstream legacy code fetched. */
```

Run from the upstream checkout:

```sh
python build/single_file_libs/combine.py -r lib -x legacy/zstd_legacy.h -o zstd.c rad-zstd-in.c
```

Copy the generated `zstd.c`, `lib/zstd.h`, `lib/zstd_errors.h`, `LICENSE`, and
`COPYING` into this directory. The combiner inlines dependent headers and records
each one with `start inlining` markers. The two excluded-legacy `#error` lines
are intentionally inside disabled `ZSTD_LEGACY_SUPPORT` branches. Do not enable
omitted features through compiler flags; regenerate the source if needed.
